key_insight: MAC is the first public CVR benchmark that provides conversion labels under multiple attribution mechanisms, enabling multi-attribution learning (MAL) and fair evaluation of models across attribution schemes.
problem_solved: Public conversion-rate datasets use a single attribution mechanism, blocking development and comparison of MAL methods and limiting model robustness to different attribution policies.
method: Assemble a CVR dataset and generate conversion labels for each event under multiple common attribution mechanisms (e.g., last-click, position-based, time-decay).
Define standardized benchmark tasks, splits, and evaluation metrics to compare single-attribution vs multi-attribution learning approaches.
Provide baseline models and experimental results to illustrate how MAL leverages multiple label views to improve prediction robustness and generalization.
impact: MAC unlocks research and practical development of models that are robust to attribution choice, helping practitioners build CVR predictors that generalize across different business attribution policies and ad platforms.
visual_elements: Diagram showing a user journey with conversions labeled differently under multiple attribution mechanisms (color-coded overlays).
Bar/stacked chart of dataset composition: number of events labeled per attribution mechanism and distribution across splits.
Pipeline diagram: data collection → multi-label generation → model training (single vs MAL) → evaluation metrics.
Benchmarks plot comparing performance of single-attribution models vs MAL baselines across attribution schemes.
paper_title: MAC: A Conversion Rate Prediction Benchmark Featuring Labels Under Multiple Attribution Mechanisms
paper_authors: Jinqi Wu, Sishuo Chen, Zhangming Chan, Yong Bai, Lei Zhang
